newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to complain to WTO over Indonesia car policy.
newsitem.headline: Japan to complain to WTO over Indonesia car policy.

text.p: Japan plans to file a complaint with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) over Indonesia's national car policy within a week or so, a Trade Ministry official said on Wednesday.
Indonesia's national car plan, announced earlier this year, has come under fire from Japan, the United States and the European Union as a violation of world trade rules.
In February, Indonesia gave special tax and tariff breaks to PT Putra Timor Nasional to make a "national car" in partnership with Kia Motors Corp of South Korea.
The Indonesian firm is controlled by President Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra.

Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) confirmed on Tuesday that Indonesia had not imposed any tariff on its national cars produced in South Korea when the products passed through Indonesian customs, the ministry official told reporters.
"As soon as we confirm the number and sales price of these cars, we will start the procedures for filing a complaint to the WTO within a week or so," the ministry official said on Wednesday.
Tokyo argues that the special tax treatment for PT Putra Timor Nasional breaches World Trade Organisation rules and puts rival manufacturers at a competitive disadvantage.
The United States said on Tuesday that it planned to take up the Indonesian national car issue with the WTO.
